Fill:
-- Turns a bar's fill image into a left-to-right fill that CROPS the texture instead of squashing
-- it: the image is wrapped in a clipping frame at its original rect, and only the frame's width
-- changes. Everything stays in Scale units, so it is resolution independent.
local Fill = {}

-- A plain table (a weak-keyed one can drop a live Instance key, and the bar would then get wrapped
-- a second time); entries go when the clip is destroyed.
local Wrapped = {}

-- The clip takes over the image's NAME (the image is renamed "Fill"), so existing lookups such as
-- Bar.Bar keep finding something, and Set() accepts either the clip or the image.
function Fill.Wrap(Image)
	if Wrapped[Image] then return Wrapped[Image] end
	local Clip = Instance.new("Frame")
	Clip.Name = Image.Name
	Image.Name = "Fill"
	Clip.BackgroundTransparency = 1
	Clip.ClipsDescendants = true
	Clip.ZIndex = Image.ZIndex
	local Size, Pos, Anchor = Image.Size, Image.Position, Image.AnchorPoint
	-- left edge of the original rect, in parent scale
	Clip.AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(0, Anchor.Y)
	Clip.Position = UDim2.new(Pos.X.Scale - Anchor.X * Size.X.Scale, Pos.X.Offset - Anchor.X * Size.X.Offset, Pos.Y.Scale, Pos.Y.Offset)
	Clip.Size = Size
	Clip.Parent = Image.Parent
	Image.AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(0, 0)
	Image.Position = UDim2.fromScale(0, 0)
	Image.Size = UDim2.fromScale(1, 1)
	Image.Parent = Clip
	local W = {Clip = Clip, Image = Image, Width = Size.X.Scale, Offset = Size.X.Offset}
	Wrapped[Image] = W
	Wrapped[Clip] = W
	Clip.Destroying:Once(function() Wrapped[Image], Wrapped[Clip] = nil, nil end)
	return W
end

function Fill.Set(Image, Ratio)
	local W = Fill.Wrap(Image)
	Ratio = math.clamp(Ratio ~= Ratio and 0 or Ratio, 0, 1)
	W.Clip.Size = UDim2.new(W.Width * Ratio, W.Offset * Ratio, W.Clip.Size.Y.Scale, W.Clip.Size.Y.Offset)

Pond.Format: x, z, waterTop, bedY, bedMaterial, bedPathIndex
